title: Serve a soft-serve swirl: pull the machine's lever with one hand while circling and lowering the cup under the nozzle with the other
instruction: Serve a soft-serve swirl in the sundae cup: hold the cup under the machine's nozzle with one hand and pull the lever down with the other. While it flows, move the cup in circles under the nozzle and lower it slowly, so the serve is laid in rings stacked up to the cup's rim. When the cup is full, let the lever up, then set the cup down upright on the green mat.
context: Almost everyone has watched a soft serve pulled at an ice-cream counter or a fast-food restaurant: one hand holds the lever down while the other circles and lowers the cup under a continuous stream at the right speed and height, so the serve lands in neat stacked rings instead of a heap, a spill or a jammed nozzle. Soft-serve machines are standard commercial equipment in fast-food restaurants and ice-cream shops, so the machine's cost reflects ordinary commercial pricing, not specialist or custom equipment.
setup: Station table (110 x 130 cm); positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases projected onto the table (x forward away from the robot, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Countertop soft-serve machine with a draw lever and a self-closing valve (for example a Spaceman 6210-C, about $6,400 new), brushed steel, fixed to the table: a lower body (x 40.5 to 65, y -21 to +10, 28 cm tall) and a head above it (x 30.2 to 65, same y, from 28 to 80 cm), leaving a cup space under the head 28 cm tall and 10 cm deep. Nozzle: a square chrome spout 3.3 cm across (2.5 cm bore), 3 cm long, on the vertical axis x 33, y -9, its tip 25 cm above the table. Draw lever: pivot on the head's front face at x 29.4, y +6, 32 cm up; a 10 cm black arm (1.4 cm square) points toward the robot, ending in a red knob (3 x 2.6 x 2.6 cm) centred at x 18.4, y +6, 32 cm up. A spring holds the lever up (about 0.6 N at the knob, 3 N at the stop); pulled down it opens the valve from 12 deg, fully at 25 deg, with a stop at 32 deg; letting it up closes the valve. Soft serve comes out as a 1.9 cm round strand (soft serve at about 0.74 g/cm3, 2.1 g per cm) at up to 5 cm/s with the lever fully down. A full cup is one 40 cm serving (about 84 g, 8 s at full flow). Cup: a rigid white plastic sundae cup, 50 g, 6 cm deep, 6.4 cm across inside at the bottom and 7.0 cm at the rim, 2.5 mm wall, standing upright with its centre at x 26, y -18. Mat: a green rubber disc, 12 cm diameter, 2 mm thick, centred at x 17, y -9.
scoring: Scored at the end of the episode, from video, a ruler and a kitchen scale. 0 if, at any time, the cup tips more than 30 deg from upright, any serve rests on the table (within 3 mm of it) outside the cup, or serve flows while the cup stands on the table; also 0 if the cup is overfilled (the serve in it weighs more than 100 g, from weighing the cup before and after), and 0 if, after the serving is finished, any serve is outside the cup: below the rim outside the cup's wall, or above the rim more than 1.5 cm out beyond the rim line, or on the machine. The serving is finished when the lever is up and the serve has broken off the nozzle. Otherwise, if it is not finished: 0.1 once any serve has come out, else 0. Once it is finished, with all the serve in the cup: rings = net turns the serve's centre line makes around the cup's axis in one direction (from the overhead and wrist videos); top = height of the top of the serve relative to the rim. 2.5 or more rings and the top no lower than 1 cm below the rim, with the cup standing on the mat (its centre within 2.8 cm of the mat's centre), within 10 deg of upright, neither gripper within 2 cm of it and the lever up (less than 12 deg down), all held for 1 continuous second = 1.0 (success, the episode ends); 2.5 or more rings and the top no lower than 1 cm below the rim otherwise = 0.75; 1.5 or more rings = 0.5; fewer = 0.25.
reset_notes: Mix: a liquid vanilla soft-serve mix, kept below 5 C (41 F) in the machine's hopper and dispensed at -8 to -7 C (18 to 20 F); start each trial only when the machine shows it is ready to serve. Read the score within 2 minutes of the serving, before the serve slumps. Between trials: empty and wipe the cup (or use an identical spare), wipe the nozzle, let the lever up, and stand the cup on its mark at x 26, y -18. Protecting the rig: cover the table around the machine and the mat with a wipe-clean food-safe sheet; the grippers touch only the cup and the lever knob, so serve reaches them only after a spill; wipe the grippers, the knob and the sheet with a damp cloth after any trial in which serve touched them.
fidelity: Serve: a 43 cm strand of 36 rigid 1.2 cm capsules (1.9 cm thick, 90 g in all; the last 3 cm stays in the machine) with weak bending springs, drawn as one smooth tube. Stickiness: a piece is welded to the cup where it lands (just out of the nozzle within 1.2 cm of the floor or serve below, or touching the cup or stuck serve below 20 cm/s); no flow, melting or squash. The feed is a force-limited piston; the valve is scripted from the lever angle. The sim's machine holds one 40 cm serving: letting the lever up once it is all out breaks the stream off at the nozzle (letting it up earlier only pauses the flow), and holding the lever down more than 1.5 s after it is all out stands in for the overflow a real machine would give (about 16 g more, past the 100 g limit) and scores 0. The cup and machine are rigid. Physics 240 Hz, control 20 Hz.
